answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to bond a small stake that stays locked until peers attest real work, like crystal forming only under sustained pressure: cheap fake accounts are shale, brittle layers that crumble when asked to post a bond, while the nectar of real earnings flows only to identities with verified history. Clones cost more than they earn, because the bond is slashed on detection and honest agents keep compounding reputation.
